label: Week of October 2, 2026
intro: Three options this week, from most hands-off cooking to least effort overall. Each one is a breakfast, two mains that swap between lunch and dinner, and a snack, all made in one prep day.

plans.name: Mediterranean & Italian
plans.blurb: Lemon-herb chicken bowls with quinoa and hummus, and a turkey-lentil bolognese. The sous vide and Instant Pot do the cooking; you mostly wait.
pantry: Greek seasoning (or oregano, garlic powder, lemon pepper)

recipes.name: Spinach & Feta Egg Bites + a Pear
recipes.summary: Starbucks-style egg bites, cooked in jars in the sous vide. Velvety, and they reheat in 60 seconds.
recipes.freezeTip: Freezes for up to 3 months in the jar. Thaw overnight in the fridge, or microwave from frozen for 2–3 minutes.
steps: Heat the sous vide water to 77°C (171°F).
Thaw and squeeze the spinach. Blend {{eggbites}} until smooth (blender or stick blender).
Set a 500 mL wide-mouth jar on the scale, zero it, and pour in your egg bite amount. Repeat for each day. Close the lids finger-tight.
Lower the jars in and cook 1½ hours. Cool on the counter 20 minutes, then refrigerate.
To eat: lid off, microwave 60–90 seconds. Have the pear on the side.
notes: Cottage cheese is the secret: it doubles the protein and makes them creamy, not rubbery.

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Quinoa Bowls
recipes.summary: Sous vide lemon-oregano chicken, quinoa, chickpeas, air-fried peppers and broccoli, with a scoop of hummus.
recipes.freezeTip: Freezes for up to 3 months. The quinoa and chicken hold up well; the peppers soften a little. Hummus freezes fine.
steps: Chicken: season {{chicken}} with Greek seasoning, a splash of lemon juice and salt. Bag it in a single layer and sous vide at 65°C (149°F) for 2–4 hours. Slice once it's cool enough to handle.

Quinoa: rinse {{quinoa}} and put it in the Instant Pot with 1.75 times its weight in water (weigh it straight in). High pressure 1 minute, natural release 10 minutes. Fluff and spread on a tray to cool.
Veg: toss {{veg}} straight from frozen. Air fry at 200°C (400°F) for 15–18 minutes, shaking once. Do it in two loads if your basket is small.
Drain and rinse {{chickpeas}}.
Build each container: chicken, quinoa, chickpeas, veg, and the hummus in a corner (or a small lidded cup).
notes: Don't feel like quinoa? Microwave quinoa pouches work. Weigh the same amount.

recipes.name: Turkey & Lentil Bolognese with Whole-Wheat Rotini
recipes.summary: A dump-and-go Instant Pot sauce made with jarred marinara. The lentils and spinach add fibre without any chopping.
recipes.freezeTip: Freezes for up to 3 months. Bolognese and pasta both reheat like new.
steps: Instant Pot on Sauté. Brown the turkey with a little oil and 1 tsp Italian seasoning, breaking it up, about 6 minutes.
Add the drained lentils and frozen spinach, then pour the marinara over the top with 125 mL water. Don't stir. Sauce on top avoids the burn warning. Sauce batch: {{sauce}}.
High pressure 8 minutes, quick release, then stir.
Pasta: boil {{pasta}} for 1 minute less than the box says. Drain and toss with a teaspoon of oil. Sit down while it boils.
Each container: pasta, sauce on top, parmesan sprinkled over.
notes: The sauce batch is sized in half-recipes, so you may have a portion or two extra. Freeze them as backups for bad days.

recipes.name: Greek Yogurt Berry Chia Cups
recipes.summary: Yogurt, frozen berries and chia layered in jars. The berries thaw into a jammy layer by morning.
recipes.freezeTip: Yogurt goes grainy when frozen. Keep these in the fridge and eat them within 5 days.
steps: Into each jar, in this order: berries, then chia, then yogurt.
Lid on, fridge. Stir before eating.
notes: Add a drizzle of honey if you want it sweeter. It isn't counted, but a teaspoon is only about 20 kcal.

steps.text: Fill a big pot with water, clip on the sous vide, set 65°C (149°F).
Season and bag the chicken: {{A-m1.chicken}}. Lower it in once the water is up to heat. It can stay 2–4 hours, so there's no rush.
Instant Pot quinoa: {{A-m1.quinoa}} + 1.75× its weight in water. High pressure 1 minute, natural release 10 minutes, then spread it on a tray to cool.
Rest. Everything is cooking itself.

prep.name: Session 2: bolognese, veg and egg bites

steps.text: Instant Pot bolognese: {{A-m2.sauce}}. Brown the turkey, layer the rest in, sauce on top, high pressure 8 minutes.
Air fryer, straight from frozen: {{A-m1.veg}}. 200°C for 15–18 minutes, shake once.
Put the pasta on to boil: {{A-m2.pasta}}. Sit while it cooks.
Chicken out of the bath (it's fine in its bags in the fridge). Turn the sous vide up to 77°C (171°F).
Egg bites: blend {{A-b.eggbites}}. Weigh into {{days}} jars (amount on the portion card), lids finger-tight, 1½ hours in the bath.
Rest while the egg bites cook and everything cools.
Set up at the table with the scale and containers. Slice the chicken, then build each container from the portion card. Zero the scale between each item.
Snack cups for the first {{keepDays}} days: berries, chia, yogurt.
Label: days 1–{{fridgeDays}} go in the fridge, the rest in the freezer. Move one day's worth from freezer to fridge each night.

plans.name: Tex-Mex
plans.blurb: Chipotle-lime chicken burrito bowls and an Instant Pot turkey chili, both over one batch of brown rice, plus an egg bake you cut into squares for breakfast.

recipes.name: Tex-Mex Egg Bake Squares + Tortilla
recipes.summary: One pan of eggs, black beans, peppers, salsa and cheddar, cut into squares. Wrap a square in a warm tortilla and it's a breakfast burrito.
recipes.freezeTip: Freezes for up to 3 months. Freeze the squares; keep the tortillas in the cupboard.
steps: Oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a 9×13 pan (an 8×8 for a half batch).
Whisk the eggs, egg whites and salsa in a big bowl. Stir in the drained beans, frozen peppers and cheddar. Batch: {{eggbake}}.
Pour into the pan and bake 40–50 minutes, until the middle no longer jiggles.
Cool, then cut into 16 squares (4 × 4), or 8 for a half batch in the 8×8 pan. Each is about 115 g.
To eat: microwave the square 60 seconds and fold it into a tortilla.
notes: Squares freeze well. Wrap two together so a morning's portion is one grab.

recipes.name: Chipotle-Lime Chicken Burrito Bowls
recipes.summary: Sous vide chicken thighs shredded with lime, over brown rice with black beans, corn and peppers. Salsa and a little cheddar on top.
recipes.freezeTip: Freezes for up to 3 months. Rice and chicken hold up well; the salsa gets a bit watery.

components.name: Frozen corn & pepper strips (straight in, they cook on reheat)

steps: Chicken: rub {{chicken}} with 1 tbsp chipotle or taco seasoning and a splash of lime juice. Bag and sous vide at 70°C (158°F) for 2–4 hours, then shred with two forks (sitting down).
Rice: rinse {{rice}}, then Instant Pot it with 1.6 times its weight in water. High pressure 22 minutes, natural release 10 minutes.
Drain and rinse {{beans}}.
Each container: rice, beans, chicken, a handful of frozen corn and peppers straight from the bag, then salsa and cheddar.
notes: The frozen veg goes in raw-frozen. It steams itself when you reheat, so there's nothing to cook.

recipes.name: Instant Pot Turkey & Two-Bean Chili
recipes.summary: Ground turkey, black and kidney beans, tomatoes and salsa, done in 10 minutes under pressure. Served over the same brown rice.
recipes.freezeTip: Chili is one of the best foods to freeze. Up to 3 months.
steps: Instant Pot on Sauté: brown the turkey with a packet of chili seasoning, about 6 minutes.
Add the drained beans and frozen peppers, then pour the tomatoes and salsa on top. Don't stir. Chili batch: {{chili}}.
High pressure 10 minutes, natural release 10 minutes, then stir.
Each container: rice, chili over it, cheddar on top.
notes: Sized in half-recipes. Extra portions are freezer backups.

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese, Berries & Pepitas
recipes.summary: Creamy, sweet-salty and high in protein. The berries and pumpkin seeds bring the fibre and crunch.
recipes.freezeTip: Cottage cheese goes watery when frozen. Keep these in the fridge for up to 5 days.
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into small containers with the frozen berries on top. They thaw by the next day.
Keep the pumpkin seeds in a separate bag and sprinkle them on when you eat, so they stay crunchy.

steps.text: Sous vide to 70°C (158°F).
Season and bag the chicken thighs: {{B-m1.chicken}}. Into the bath for 2–4 hours.
Instant Pot, all the rice for both mains: {{B-m1.rice+B-m2.rice}} + 1.6× its weight in water. High pressure 22 minutes, natural release 10 minutes.
Rest.
Oven to 180°C (350°F). Spread the rice on a tray to cool.
Egg bake: {{B-b.eggbake}}. Whisk, stir, pour into the pan, and bake 40–50 minutes.
Instant Pot chili: {{B-m2.chili}}. Brown the turkey, layer the rest in, high pressure 10 minutes, natural release.
Rest while it all cooks and cools.
Shred the chicken with two forks (or a hand mixer on low, in a bowl).
Cut the egg bake into squares of about 115 g each (4 × 4 in a 9×13 pan).
Build the containers from the portion card. Zero the scale between each item.
Snack cups for the first {{keepDays}} days. Label: days 1–{{fridgeDays}} fridge, the rest freezer.

plans.name: Asian-Inspired, Least Effort
plans.blurb: Teriyaki chicken bowls made with store-bought rotisserie chicken, and Korean-style beef bowls with kimchi. No-cook overnight oats for breakfast. The lowest-effort plan: about 35 minutes of actual work.

recipes.name: Berry Overnight Oats with Greek Yogurt
recipes.summary: Oats, milk, chia and frozen berries mixed in one bowl, then topped with Greek yogurt. Nothing to cook.
recipes.freezeTip: Freezes for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and stir; it's a little looser after thawing.
steps: In your biggest bowl, stir together {{oats}} with a big pinch of cinnamon.
Weigh the oat base into each jar, then spoon the yogurt on top.
Eat cold, or microwave 90 seconds and stir.
notes: Days 5–7 freeze fine. Move a jar to the fridge the night before.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Chicken & Edamame Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Rotisserie chicken, brown rice, frozen stir-fry veg and edamame, with bottled teriyaki. Pure assembly.
recipes.freezeTip: Freezes for up to 3 months. Add a splash of water before reheating the rice.
steps: Pull the meat off {{chicken}} and throw out the skin. Do this sitting down. Pre-pulled rotisserie chicken or plain cooked chicken strips skip this step.
Rice: cooked in the Instant Pot along with the other main's rice (see the prep tab).
Each container: rice, chicken, a handful each of frozen veg and edamame straight from the bag, then teriyaki drizzled over.
notes: Rotisserie chicken is salty. If you're watching sodium, go easy on the teriyaki.

recipes.name: Korean-Style Beef & Broccoli Bowls
recipes.summary: Lean ground beef browned with bottled bulgogi sauce, over brown rice with broccoli. Kimchi on the side when you eat.
recipes.freezeTip: Freezes for up to 3 months. Keep the kimchi in its jar, not the container.
steps: Instant Pot on Sauté (or a skillet): brown the beef, breaking it up, about 8 minutes. Spoon off any fat. Batch: {{beef}}.
Stir in the Korean BBQ sauce and let it bubble for a minute.
Each container: rice, beef, frozen broccoli straight from the bag.
When you eat: reheat, then add kimchi on the side.
notes: The air fryer works for ground beef too: 200°C for 8–10 minutes, stirring once. Less standing at the stove.

recipes.name: Salted Edamame + Clementines
recipes.summary: Warm or cold edamame with flaky salt, and a clementine or two.
recipes.freezeTip: Edamame starts out frozen, so freezing the portions changes nothing.
steps: Portion frozen edamame into small containers and keep them frozen. Each one goes from freezer to fridge the night before.
To eat: 60–90 seconds in the microwave (or eat it cold), sprinkle with salt. Clementines on the side.

steps.text: Instant Pot, all the rice for both mains: {{C-m1.rice+C-m2.rice}} + 1.6× its weight in water. High pressure 22 minutes, natural release 10 minutes.
Overnight oats: stir together {{C-b.oats}} and set aside.
Pull the rotisserie chicken: {{C-m1.chicken}}.
When the rice is out: brown the beef in the Instant Pot on Sauté (or air fryer), then stir in the sauce: {{C-m2.beef}}.
Rest while things cool.
At the table with the scale: build all the containers from the portion card. Frozen veg and edamame go in straight from the bag.
Label: days 1–{{fridgeDays}} fridge, the rest freezer.
